O.content: The blue circular mark is higher on the page than the red square mark.
The left vertical label is blue and reads "0-19 years"; the right vertical label is red and reads "20-39 years".
The title reads "0-19 years vs 20-39 years".

B.text: If the blue circular series is the 0-19 years series and the red square series is the 20-39 years series, and both series use the same vertically comparable population scale, then the series mark higher on the page at the same year encodes the larger population. Under the task instruction, open the follow-up record for that larger cohort.
B.conditions: Applies to the 2012 marks only; requires that the two colored axes/series are on a common or directly comparable population scale.

O.content: Separate colored vertical labels appear on the left and right sides of the plot: blue "0-19 years" and red "20-39 years".
No numeric y-axis tick labels are visibly printed on either side of the plot.
The blue circular mark is higher on the page than the red square mark.

B.text: If the differently colored left and right axes can use independent, unshown, or non-comparable scales, then screen-space height of the blue and red 2012 marks alone does not establish which cohort has the larger population. Without another public dashboard value or scale bridge, the comparison is unresolved; routine archive is the available non-cohort routing option.
B.conditions: Applies because the chart visibly has separate blue and red y-axis labels and no printed y-axis tick values.
